bug_semantics: A local GLX client can send ChangeDrawableAttributes with a request buffer shorter than the numAttribs count claims. Both native and byte-swapped dispatchers compute the required size but compare it in the wrong direction: expected_words < client->req_len. That rejects an overlong request while allowing an undersized one. The native dispatcher then passes req + 1 to DoChangeDrawableAttributes, whose numAttribs loop reads two CARD32 values per claimed attribute beyond the request buffer, disclosing adjacent server memory; the byte-swapped path first swaps the same client-controlled number of words in place, providing an out-of-bounds write path for byte-swapped clients, which the advisory says are disabled by default.
flaw_origin: Commit 402b329c3aa8ddbebaa1f593306a02d4cd6fed26 deliberately replaced REQUEST_FIXED_SIZE in glx/glxcmds.c and glx/glxcmdsswap.c with a Mesa compatibility workaround. For ChangeDrawableAttributes it wrote the manual '< client->req_len' comparison, reversing the required rejection condition and creating the undersized-request bypass. The immediate parent used the correct REQUEST_FIXED_SIZE macro in both dispatchers.
ai_marker: absent: the exact BIC commit object for 402b329c3aa8ddbebaa1f593306a02d4cd6fed26 has human author and committer Julien Cristau <jcristau@debian.org>; its only trailers are Reported-by, Signed-off-by, and Reviewed-by. It has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, Assisted-by, AI-tool trailer, or bot identity.
evidence: The first-party X.Org advisory at https://lists.x.org/archives/xorg-announce/2026-June/003702.html identifies the GLX ChangeDrawableAttributes out-of-bounds read/write, says the write requires byte-swapped clients, states that X.Org Server before 21.1.23 and Xwayland before 24.1.12 are affected, and links the direct fix https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/xorg/xserver/-/commit/6d459e4daf715bea8abdafa8fb130be2f8a1d145 (merged through first-party MR https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/xorg/xserver/-/merge_requests/2228). The fix message itself names 402b329c3aa8ddbebaa1f593306a02d4cd6fed26 as the commit being effectively reverted. In the clone, git log -L 1501,1514:glx/glxcmds.c at the BIC and git log -S client->req_len over parent..BIC both identify only 402b329c3aa8ddbebaa1f593306a02d4cd6fed26 for the flawed block; the BIC is a one-parent, non-squash commit and its diff adds the same reversed check to glx/glxcmds.c and glx/glxcmdsswap.c. Direct-parent tree verification at 1137c11be0f82049d28024eaf963c6f76e0d4334 shows REQUEST_FIXED_SIZE(xGLXChangeDrawableAttributesReq, req->numAttribs << 3) at glx/glxcmds.c:1501 and glx/glxcmdsswap.c:479, so the vulnerable manual '< client->req_len' lines are absent. At the BIC, glx/glxcmds.c:1469-1488 shows DoChangeDrawableAttributes indexing attribs[i * 2] and attribs[i * 2 + 1], and glx/glxcmdsswap.c:479-483 shows the bypass followed by __GLX_SWAP_INT_ARRAY(attribs, req->numAttribs << 1). Tag ancestry places the BIC in xorg-server-1.10.0 and in all four boundary tags checked. Source-tree checks show the flawed comparator in xorg-server-21.1.22 at glx/glxcmds.c:1531-1533 and glx/glxcmdsswap.c:443-445 and in xwayland-24.1.11 at the same lines; xorg-server-21.1.23 and xwayland-24.1.12 instead contain REQUEST_FIXED_SIZE at glx/glxcmds.c:1525 and glx/glxcmdsswap.c:443. The release-branch fixes are 94341bd715d62ba8da4c1851f517018996da1af8 for xorg-server-21.1.23 and 901da57abfde6bf2ae33859c2dd47b45d6dd5871 for xwayland-24.1.12; git patch-id --stable gives identical patch id 90e3f8d28381bc8c44e9446345e273f877cdaa9f for both and for direct fix 6d459e4daf715bea8abdafa8fb130be2f8a1d145. The BIC is available first-party at https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/xorg/xserver/-/commit/402b329c3aa8ddbebaa1f593306a02d4cd6fed26.
reasoning: The vulnerability is not the original attribute loop by itself: before the BIC, both dispatchers coupled numAttribs to the actual request length with REQUEST_FIXED_SIZE. The 2011 Mesa workaround is the smallest causal change because it alone disabled that correct check and introduced the reversed manual comparison in both externally reachable dispatch paths; git history traces those exact lines to that commit, and the immediate parent proves they were absent while the safe macro was present. The BIC predates and is an ancestor of the vulnerable release boundaries, while the direct fix restores REQUEST_FIXED_SIZE and patch-equivalent backports are present in exactly the first fixed X.Org Server and Xwayland tags named by the advisory. AI attribution is judged only from the BIC commit object. Its human identities and trailers contain no AI marker, so the causal verdict is NOT_AI; the Assisted-by marker on the 2026 fix is irrelevant to attribution of the 2011 BIC.
